subject: BENCHSARGENT
name: White Ships — transparent hull planes and warm tackle

styleSelection.reason: Pure watercolor: luminous cool value planes, reserved cream paper and selective dark painted fittings. Broad connected washes, dry shaped middle planes and cross-region shadow glazes; no drawing medium.

ships.central-hull.reason: The curved blue-gray bow has broad transparent planes and a firm left contour; soften selected turning edges with clean water while keeping the dark waterline sharp.

ships.right-hull.reason: The right hull is mostly warm paper and pale gray-blue facets, with crisp dark oval fittings; paint around the light plane and add fittings after full drying.

ships.tackle.reason: Ochre ropes, the anchor and slender upright supports have connected shaped strokes and broken warm highlights; paint on dry paper without ink or uniform hatching.

ships.water.reason: Green-blue water and reflected hull shadows are connected transparent planes; retain broken horizontal cream lights and finish the deepest contact shadows on dry paper.

ships.background.reason: The narrow upper-left background is a pale blue-gray wash behind crisp tackle; a dry-start wash preserves the adjacent structural edges and selective clean-water softening loses distant edges.

families.referenceCue: Large cool concave bow: broad pale blue-gray wash first, two transparent shaped middle layers on dry paper, darkest curved left edge and keel shadow last; preserve scattered pale reflections.
Cream-white right ship: luminous hull face, pale cool angular reflections, two dark oval fittings near the top; reserve the connected near-paper plane and keep the fittings crisp.
Left foreground anchor and ochre ropes have warm connected bodies with tapered irregular edges; ochre uprights cross the cool hulls and should stay legible as paint.
Green-blue water under the white ships, a darker continuous contact shadow at the central keel and broken pale horizontal reflection strokes; broad underwash then dry glazes crossing hull and water.
Pale gray-blue open slivers behind the left upright tackle; one connected light wash with only selected distant edges softened, no tiled sky or outlines.
